Methods for zinbreg objects

Source: R/methods.R
zinbreg-methods.Rd

Standard S3 methods for fits from zinbreg().

Usage

# S3 method for class 'zinbreg'
print(x, digits = max(3L, getOption("digits") - 3L), ...)

# S3 method for class 'zinbreg'
coef(object, model = c("full", "count", "zero"), ...)

# S3 method for class 'zinbreg'
vcov(object, model = c("full", "count", "zero"), ...)

# S3 method for class 'zinbreg'
logLik(object, ...)

# S3 method for class 'zinbreg'
nobs(object, ...)

# S3 method for class 'zinbreg'
fitted(object, ...)

# S3 method for class 'zinbreg'
residuals(object, type = c("pearson", "response"), ...)

# S3 method for class 'zinbreg'
predict(object, newdata, type = c("response", "count", "zero"), ...)

# S3 method for class 'zinbreg'
summary(object, ...)

# S3 method for class 'summary.zinbreg'
print(x, digits = max(3L, getOption("digits") - 3L), ...)

Arguments

x, object

An object of class "zinbreg" (or "summary.zinbreg" for the print method of a summary).

digits

Number of significant digits to print.

...

Further arguments (ignored).

model

Which part of the model: "full" (default), "count" or "zero".

type

For residuals: "pearson" (default) or "response". For predict: "response", "count" or "zero".

newdata

Optional data frame for predict.

Value

See nbreg-methods for the common methods. summary returns an object of class "summary.zinbreg" with coefficient tables for the count and zero parts.

Details

coef and vcov return the coefficients (and their covariance matrix) of the count part, the zero part, or both ("full", with names count_* and zero_*, as in pscl::zeroinfl()). The covariance of the full fit including Log(theta) is stored in the fitted object as vcov.

For predict, type = "response" gives the marginal mean \((1-\pi)\mu\), "count" the NB mean \(\mu\), and "zero" the structural-zero probability \(\pi\). Pearson residuals use the ZINB variance \((1-\pi)\mu\{1 + \mu(\pi + 1/\theta)\}\).

Examples

set.seed(1)
n <- 400
d <- data.frame(x = rnorm(n), z = rnorm(n))
pz <- plogis(-1 + 0.8 * d$z)
d$y <- ifelse(runif(n) < pz, 0, rnbinom(n, mu = exp(1 + 0.5 * d$x), size = 2))
fit <- zinbreg(y ~ x | z, data = d)
summary(fit)
#> 
#> Call:
#> zinbreg(formula = y ~ x | z, data = d)
#> 
#> Count model coefficients (negative binomial with log link):
#>             Estimate Std. Error z value Pr(>|z|)    
#> (Intercept)  1.06580    0.07757  13.740  < 2e-16 ***
#> x            0.46894    0.06501   7.213 5.47e-13 ***
#> 
#> Zero-inflation model coefficients (binomial with logit link):
#>             Estimate Std. Error z value Pr(>|z|)    
#> (Intercept)  -1.1858     0.2936  -4.039 5.38e-05 ***
#> z             0.9022     0.2132   4.231 2.33e-05 ***
#> ---
#> Signif. codes:  0 '***' 0.001 '**' 0.01 '*' 0.05 '.' 0.1 ' ' 1
#> 
#> Theta: 1.523  (SE 0.327)
#> Log(theta): 0.4209  (SE 0.2146)
#> Log-likelihood: -768.513 on 5 Df;  AIC: 1547.03
#> Number of observations: 400;  EM iterations: 61
coef(fit, model = "zero")
#> (Intercept)           z 
#>  -1.1858462   0.9021801 
head(predict(fit, type = "zero"))
#>         1         2         3         4         5         6 
#> 0.4460837 0.6281704 0.1506057 0.1767564 0.1734525 0.1787621 
predict(fit, newdata = data.frame(x = 0, z = 0), type = "response")
#>        1 
#> 2.223808
